response.answer:
We’ll keep **Accounting — Bachelor of Accounting** as our subject.

- Offered full-time or part-time through Flexible Learning
- In-person at Burnaby Campus
- Curriculum includes **FMGT 8911 Strategic Performance Management**, seven Advanced Technical Specialty electives, and 36 General Education credits, including **LIBS 7001 Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 Applied Ethics**
- Optional work terms are available to full-time domestic students
- Designed as academic preparation toward the CPA pathway; it does not itself award the CPA designation

[View the Bachelor of Accounting program](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

request.instructions: You are Asteris, an academic advisor for the institution. The question has been routed as PROGRAM_INFO. Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Response-depth policy (expanded): Add useful new detail about the active subject. Do not repeat the prior result card or opening summary. Use a short overview followed by the most relevant details. Write like a concise professional academic advisor. Use natural transitions and plain language around exact program names, course names, and codes. Do not restate the question, narrate tool use, or repeat information from the immediately preceding assistant turn unless the student asks for repetition. Avoid generic disclaimers and the phrase 'available Asteris data' when a specific boundary can be stated. Use bullets only when three or more parallel items are genuinely useful; never dump a curriculum or catalog unless requested or necessary. For comparisons, state the meaningful differences and shared facts once. For frustration plus a substantive question, briefly acknowledge the problem and answer it. For a clear stop, stop. Describe evidence boundaries precisely: distinguish a verified fact, a conditional rule, missing or unpublished information, and a point requiring institutional confirmation. Never convert unknown information into a likely yes or no, and never guarantee admission, transfer credit, licensing, placement, employment, or permits. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. When program evidence includes academic_scope_boundaries, keep credential-award evidence separate from later-level progression requirements. A continuation rule for a later level is not a condition for an earlier credential unless the stored credential-award evidence explicitly says it is. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Answer yes/no and discovery questions concisely unless the student asks to list, show, browse, compare, or explain. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. A level explicitly named in the current question overrides unrelated levels in history; never offer progression to another level.

content.text:
The **Bachelor of Accounting** is a 60-credit degree for graduates of Accounting, Finance, Financial Planning, or equivalent diplomas. It develops advanced technical accounting, communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills, with a maximum completion period of seven years.

Admission includes a minimum 70% diploma GPA and English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent; external diplomas are assessed individually and may require bridging.

[View full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

We’ll keep **Accounting — Bachelor of Accounting** as our subject.

- Offered full-time or part-time through Flexible Learning
- In-person at Burnaby Campus
- Curriculum includes **FMGT 8911 Strategic Performance Management**, seven Advanced Technical Specialty electives, and 36 General Education credits, including **LIBS 7001 Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 Applied Ethics**

- Designed as academic preparation toward the CPA pathway; it does not itself award the CPA designation

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Response-depth policy (short): Answer the requested fact in the first sentence. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. conversation.content: I'm exploring Accounting bachelor's degree. Please keep that as our subject.

We’ll keep **Accounting — Bachelor of Accounting** as our subject.

- Offered full-time or part-time through Flexible Learning
- In-person at Burnaby Campus
- Curriculum includes **FMGT 8911 Strategic Performance Management**, seven Advanced Technical Specialty electives, and 36 General Education credits, including **LIBS 7001 Critical Reading and Writing** and **LIBS 7002 Applied Ethics**
- Optional work terms are available to full-time domestic students
- Designed as academic preparation toward the CPA pathway; it does not itself award the CPA designation

[View the Bachelor of Accounting program](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Give me a short overview.

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is a 60-credit degree for graduates of Accounting, Finance, Financial Planning, or equivalent diplomas. It develops advanced technical accounting, communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills, with a maximum completion period of seven years.

Admission includes a minimum 70% diploma GPA and English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent; external diplomas are assessed individually and may require bridging.

[View full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc)** degree. It provides academic preparation toward the CPA pathway but does not award the CPA designation.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Where would I study?

You would study **in person at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**, whether you choose the full-time or part-time Flexible Learning option.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

response.instructions: You are Asteris, an academic advisor for the institution. The question has been routed as PROGRAM_INFO. Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Response-depth policy (short): Answer the requested fact in the first sentence. Usually stop after one or two sentences unless a condition is essential to accuracy. Write like a concise professional academic advisor. Use natural transitions and plain language around exact program names, course names, and codes. Do not restate the question, narrate tool use, or repeat information from the immediately preceding assistant turn unless the student asks for repetition. Avoid generic disclaimers and the phrase 'available Asteris data' when a specific boundary can be stated. Use bullets only when three or more parallel items are genuinely useful; never dump a curriculum or catalog unless requested or necessary. For comparisons, state the meaningful differences and shared facts once. For frustration plus a substantive question, briefly acknowledge the problem and answer it. For a clear stop, stop. Describe evidence boundaries precisely: distinguish a verified fact, a conditional rule, missing or unpublished information, and a point requiring institutional confirmation. Never convert unknown information into a likely yes or no, and never guarantee admission, transfer credit, licensing, placement, employment, or permits. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. When program evidence includes academic_scope_boundaries, keep credential-award evidence separate from later-level progression requirements. A continuation rule for a later level is not a condition for an earlier credential unless the stored credential-award evidence explicitly says it is. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Response-depth policy (short): Answer the requested fact in the first sentence. Usually stop after one or two sentences unless a condition is essential to accuracy. Write like a concise professional academic advisor. Use natural transitions and plain language around exact program names, course names, and codes. Do not restate the question, narrate tool use, or repeat information from the immediately preceding assistant turn unless the student asks for repetition. Avoid generic disclaimers and the phrase 'available Asteris data' when a specific boundary can be stated. Use bullets only when three or more parallel items are genuinely useful; never dump a curriculum or catalog unless requested or necessary. For comparisons, state the meaningful differences and shared facts once. For frustration plus a substantive question, briefly acknowledge the problem and answer it. For a clear stop, stop. Describe evidence boundaries precisely: distinguish a verified fact, a conditional rule, missing or unpublished information, and a point requiring institutional confirmation. Never convert unknown information into a likely yes or no, and never guarantee admission, transfer credit, licensing, placement, employment, or permits. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. When program evidence includes academic_scope_boundaries, keep credential-award evidence separate from later-level progression requirements. A continuation rule for a later level is not a condition for an earlier credential unless the stored credential-award evidence explicitly says it is. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Answer yes/no and discovery questions concisely unless the student asks to list, show, browse, compare, or explain. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. A level explicitly named in the current question overrides unrelated levels in history; never offer progression to another level.

request.question: What should I know before applying?

conversation.content: Give me a short overview.

The **Bachelor of Accounting** is a 60-credit degree for graduates of Accounting, Finance, Financial Planning, or equivalent diplomas. It develops advanced technical accounting, communication, interpersonal, and problem-solving skills, with a maximum completion period of seven years.

Admission includes a minimum 70% diploma GPA and English Studies 12 at 67% or equivalent; external diplomas are assessed individually and may require bridging.

[View full program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What credential does it lead to?

It leads to a **Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc)** degree. It provides academic preparation toward the CPA pathway but does not award the CPA designation.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Where would I study?

You would study **in person at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**, whether you choose the full-time or part-time Flexible Learning option.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it online or in person?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is delivered in person** at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus, with full-time and part-time Flexible Learning options.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?
It is offered **both full-time and part-time**. The part-time option is Flexible Learning, while the full-time option follows a day-stream schedule.

expectation.question: What should I know before applying?

response.answer:
Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

response.instructions: You are Asteris, an academic advisor for the institution. The question has been routed as PROGRAM_INFO. Use the provided tools for every factual claim about courses, prerequisites, eligibility, or program progress. Never guess policy. If no tool can verify a factual or policy claim, say that it cannot be verified from the available Asteris data. Internal IDs are implementation details: never ask a student for a program ID. Course codes are normal student-facing information: whenever a course is named or returned, show its display_course_code alongside its course_name. Canonical course_id values are internal lookup keys; never show them when a display_course_code is available. Program IDs may be omitted in normal prose, but when the current question explicitly requests program IDs or codes, return the real program_id. Resolve course and program names with the search tools. When eligibility or progress requires a program that has not been identified, ask naturally which program the student is taking. Never expose internal naming, resolution, or identifier terminology unless the student explicitly asks for an ID. Treat the Civil Engineering Diploma and Bachelor of Engineering as related parts of one pathway. When a requested level is shared, list it directly instead of asking which credential the student means. An explicit statement that all courses through a level were completed is sufficient completion context for a progress calculation; do not request an official outline. For course information, describe the course and its prerequisites without discussing completed-course state or eligibility. When the student asks for a course overview, reproduce the complete stored course_overview faithfully; do not summarize it or drop its final words. For prerequisites, prefer structured prerequisite rows when present. If they are absent and prerequisite_source is authoritative_raw_text, state the stored prerequisite_text exactly. Only say a course has no prerequisites when prerequisite_source is explicit_none. If the source is unknown, say the prerequisite information is unavailable; never infer 'none' merely from an empty prerequisites list. Use display_course_code in student-facing text. For program information, aggregate the curated program record, its configured program courses, and its stored source URL. For an admissions scenario, inspect the resolved program's structured ADMISSION and INTERNATIONAL rules. Separate requirements directly met by the student's stated facts, facts still missing, and non-executable or institutionally verified requirements needing human confirmation; never invent an unstored requirement. Category questions must search programs by credential. For a family/category comparison, use compare_programs and report every returned member, including unknown results; never stop at the first match. An explicit whole-catalog question overrides all prior or selected program context; report its count, program list, or distinct credentials only from the search_programs result. Electives come only from choice groups: required=false does not mean elective, and work terms are not electives. Practical-work and progression answers come only from progression requirements. Progress percentages must be quoted only from the program-progress tool and never calculated from level numbers. If requested detail is missing and a verified source_url exists, provide that link as the fallback. Do not claim that an answer is official; encourage confirmation with the institution when data is missing or ambiguous. Response-depth policy (concise_conditions): Answer the eligibility question directly, then state only the decisive verified conditions and the most useful specific next step. Write like a concise professional academic advisor. Use natural transitions and plain language around exact program names, course names, and codes. Do not restate the question, narrate tool use, or repeat information from the immediately preceding assistant turn unless the student asks for repetition. Avoid generic disclaimers and the phrase 'available Asteris data' when a specific boundary can be stated. Use bullets only when three or more parallel items are genuinely useful; never dump a curriculum or catalog unless requested or necessary. For comparisons, state the meaningful differences and shared facts once. For frustration plus a substantive question, briefly acknowledge the problem and answer it. For a clear stop, stop. Describe evidence boundaries precisely: distinguish a verified fact, a conditional rule, missing or unpublished information, and a point requiring institutional confirmation. Never convert unknown information into a likely yes or no, and never guarantee admission, transfer credit, licensing, placement, employment, or permits. Before saying a verified requirement is unavailable, call every relevant deterministic tool provided for the routed intent. Course completion state comes only from explicit statements by the student in the current conversation. Describe it as courses the student told you they completed; never mention or imply an academic profile or stored student record. Spanish uses exactly the same tools and rules as English. When a student-supplied numeric fact can be compared directly with a verified minimum, give the deterministic result and the exact difference. Qualify only whether the stated experience or credential meets the stored definition; do not say the result cannot be verified and then state the rule. Describe CMGT 8700 generically as requiring completion of required program coursework before the student's chosen final-project course; never describe CMGT 8800 as the only possible final project. Credit-based elective rules are MINIMUM_CREDITS_FROM_POOL rules, not course-count rules. Describe them as completing at least the stated credits from the approved pool. Never infer a fixed number of courses or assume every option has equal credits. Use choose-N wording only when a structured choice group provides a choose count. For every structured OR or choice group, clearly say the student chooses one option; never turn alternatives into cumulative requirements or call the set optional. A required A-or-B set is a graduation requirement even though each individual branch is an alternative. Keep ADMISSION/ENTRANCE rules separate from GRADUATION/CURRICULUM rules and never use one to answer the other. For graduation questions, call evaluate_program_curriculum when available and prefer it over individual course role labels. Department approval applies to CMGT 8800 and CMGT 8810, not CMGT 8700. CMGT 8700 itself requires the stored coursework-completion rule, two years of related work experience, an industry topic, and an industry sponsor. The standard Liberal Studies component totals 12 credits. For part-time students, explain that LIBS 7013 may be replaced by one additional 3-credit Liberal Studies elective while the other Liberal Studies requirements remain; do not call a replaceable course mandatory. A resolved active program is authoritative for every program-specific tool. When program evidence includes academic_scope_boundaries, keep credential-award evidence separate from later-level progression requirements. A continuation rule for a later level is not a condition for an earlier credential unless the stored credential-award evidence explicitly says it is. Never substitute a different program because a search is empty or irrelevant. Never invent application, acceptance, reapplication, enrolment, or document timing. For a current student asking about another pathway, explain only stored pathway and curriculum facts; label unstored transition or reapplication rules unknown. Answer yes/no and discovery questions concisely unless the student asks to list, show, browse, compare, or explain. Clearly label any inference, or omit it. Respond entirely in the language of the current student question: English. Conversation history may provide subject or entity context but must never determine or carry over the response language. Keep co-op work terms, practical-work hours, and academic level progression separate. A level explicitly named in the current question overrides unrelated levels in history; never offer progression to another level.

content.text:
Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

content.text:
The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

conversation.content: Where would I study?

You would study **in person at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus**, whether you choose the full-time or part-time Flexible Learning option.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it online or in person?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is delivered in person** at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus, with full-time and part-time Flexible Learning options.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?
It is offered **both full-time and part-time**. The part-time option is Flexible Learning, while the full-time option follows a day-stream schedule.
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: Is it online or in person?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is delivered in person** at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus, with full-time and part-time Flexible Learning options.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Is it full-time or part-time?
It is offered **both full-time and part-time**. The part-time option is Flexible Learning, while the full-time option follows a day-stream schedule.
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. The program information does not state that meeting the minimum requirements guarantees admission. BCIT must still complete the departmental pre-entry assessment, confirm your subject-sequence averages, and determine whether bridging or upgrading is required.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

expectation.question: Which details need human confirmation?
expectation.expected: Specific verification boundaries, not invented barriers.

response.answer:
The following require review or confirmation by BCIT or another authority:

- **BCIT must verify your five second-year subject-sequence averages** and whether they meet the specified grade pattern.
- The department must complete and sign the **pre-entry assessment**, including deciding whether bridging or upgrading is required.
- If your diploma is from another institution, **BCIT must assess its equivalency individually**.
- For international applicants, **IRCC makes the final PGWP decision** and study-permit validity must be confirmed.

The stated 70% diploma GPA and 67% English Studies 12 minimums can be compared directly with your grades, but meeting them does not replace the reviews above.

[View Bachelor of Accounting requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

User: Is it online or in person?
Assistant: The **Bachelor of Accounting is delivered in person** at BCIT’s Burnaby Campus, with full-time and part-time Flexible Learning options.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: Is it full-time or part-time?
Assistant: It is offered **both full-time and part-time**. The part-time option is Flexible Learning, while the full-time option follows a day-stream schedule.
User: What should I know before applying?
Assistant: Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

content.text:
The following require review or confirmation by BCIT or another authority:

- **BCIT must verify your five second-year subject-sequence averages** and whether they meet the specified grade pattern.
- The department must complete and sign the **pre-entry assessment**, including deciding whether bridging or upgrading is required.
- If your diploma is from another institution, **BCIT must assess its equivalency individually**.
- For international applicants, **IRCC makes the final PGWP decision** and study-permit validity must be confirmed.

The stated 70% diploma GPA and 67% English Studies 12 minimums can be compared directly with your grades, but meeting them does not replace the reviews above.

[View Bachelor of Accounting requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

request.question: Can you put that more simply?

conversation.content: Is it full-time or part-time?
It is offered **both full-time and part-time**. The part-time option is Flexible Learning, while the full-time option follows a day-stream schedule.
What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. The program information does not state that meeting the minimum requirements guarantees admission. BCIT must still complete the departmental pre-entry assessment, confirm your subject-sequence averages, and determine whether bridging or upgrading is required.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

The following require review or confirmation by BCIT or another authority:

- **BCIT must verify your five second-year subject-sequence averages** and whether they meet the specified grade pattern.
- The department must complete and sign the **pre-entry assessment**, including deciding whether bridging or upgrading is required.
- If your diploma is from another institution, **BCIT must assess its equivalency individually**.
- For international applicants, **IRCC makes the final PGWP decision** and study-permit validity must be confirmed.

The stated 70% diploma GPA and 67% English Studies 12 minimums can be compared directly with your grades, but meeting them does not replace the reviews above.

[View Bachelor of Accounting requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

User: Is it full-time or part-time?

User: What should I know before applying?
Assistant: Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: What about international applicants?
Assistant: The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements

conversation.content: What should I know before applying?

Before applying to the **Bachelor of Accounting**, confirm that you have:

- An Accounting, Finance, or Financial Planning diploma from BCIT—or an external equivalent assessed individually
- At least a **70% diploma GPA**
- **English Studies 12 at 67%**, or an equivalent
- Five second-year subject-sequence averages normally at **65%**, with no more than two between 62% and 65%

BCIT must confirm the subject-sequence averages and complete a signed departmental pre-entry assessment; external diplomas may require bridging or upgrading. If you are an international applicant, a valid study permit is required before starting.

Your next step is to arrange the departmental pre-entry assessment and have your diploma equivalency reviewed if it is from another institution.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
What about international applicants?

The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Does that guarantee admission?

No. The program information does not state that meeting the minimum requirements guarantees admission. BCIT must still complete the departmental pre-entry assessment, confirm your subject-sequence averages, and determine whether bridging or upgrading is required.

[View admission details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
Which details need human confirmation?

The following require review or confirmation by BCIT or another authority:

- **BCIT must verify your five second-year subject-sequence averages** and whether they meet the specified grade pattern.
- The department must complete and sign the **pre-entry assessment**, including deciding whether bridging or upgrading is required.
- If your diploma is from another institution, **BCIT must assess its equivalency individually**.
- For international applicants, **IRCC makes the final PGWP decision** and study-permit validity must be confirmed.

The stated 70% diploma GPA and 67% English Studies 12 minimums can be compared directly with your grades, but meeting them does not replace the reviews above.

[View Bachelor of Accounting requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
Can you put that more simply?

Simply put: **you can check your basic grades yourself, but BCIT must assess your diploma, subject averages, and any required upgrading.** If you’re an international applicant, **IRCC makes the final permit and PGWP decisions**.

[View Bachelor of Accounting details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)

User: What about international applicants?
Assistant: The **Bachelor of Accounting is available to international applicants**.

- You need a valid BCIT study permit before starting.
- The optional work terms **FMGT 7610 – Workplace Education Workterm 1** and **FMGT 7620 – Workplace Education Workterm 2** are not available to international students.
- Bachelor’s graduates may apply for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP), but they must meet all IRCC requirements and final approval rests with IRCC.

[View international applicant details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/accounting-bachelor-of-accounting-full-time-part-time-8630bacc/)
User: Does that guarantee admission?
Assistant: No. The program information does not state that meeting the minimum requirements guarantees admission. BCIT must still complete the departmental pre-entry assessment, confirm your subject-sequence averages, and determine whether bridging or upgrading is required.

- **BCIT must verify your five second-year subject-sequence averages** and whether they meet the specified grade pattern.

program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Accounting program offers an academic credential leading to a Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) designation. Choose between part-time Flexible Learning or full-time day stream options. Apply today to develop essential technical, communication, and problem-solving skills for success in the accounting field. Delivery: in person. See details . If you have completed a BCIT Accounting , Finance , or Financial Planning diploma, you can earn your Bachelor of Accounting (BAcc) at BCIT. This degree will provide you with an academic credential leading to a CPA (Chartered Professional Accountant ) designation, a MPAcc (Master of Professional Accounting) , or an MBA program. Students completing this program will acquire the key technical, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills demanded by employers. The BCIT model: fast, flexible and effective BCIT’s Bachelor of Accounting is offered as: Flexible Learning: The flexible part-time program allows you to maintain your career and study at the same time. You can register course by course, and apply for admission to the program any time. Or Full-Time Day Stream: This program is offered on a full-time basis for those students who want to accelerate their completion of the program. The program starts every September and January. International study BCIT offers a number of international study opportunities that helps students gain a global perspective of the economy, culture, government, and everyday life of the country they study in. You could participate in a summer field school or complete an international degree. Learn more about studying abroad . Next up Entrance Requirements
